Fact.Description: The primary filer used by Form 8919 attribution guards
The secondary filer used by Form 8919 attribution guards

Fact.Name: The four printed Form 8919 reason codes
Fact.Description:
Column (c)'s option set, which is CLOSED and printed: A, C, G and H, and no others. The option values are the printed letters themselves, lower-cased for this dictionary's enum convention, because the code IS the value a filer enters in the column rather than a label for something else.
A — "I filed Form SS-8 and received a determination letter stating that I am an employee of this firm." C — "I received other correspondence from the IRS stating that I am an employee." The instruction glosses this as the section 530 case: the filer was determined to be an employee but the employer was granted relief from employment taxes under section 530 of the Revenue Act of 1978 (lines 95-100). G — "I filed Form SS-8 with the IRS and haven't received a reply." This is also the catch-all the instruction directs a filer to when none of the others fit: "If none of the reason codes apply to you, but you believe you should have been treated as an employee, enter reason code G and file Form SS-8 on or before the date you file your tax return." H — "I received a Form W-2 and a Form 1099-MISC and/or 1099-NEC from this firm for 2025."
THERE IS NO B, D, E OR F. The printed set skips those letters and this option set does not invent them.
AN ENUM, NOT FOUR BOOLEANS, and the discriminator is printed: "Enter only one reason code on each line" (lines 87-88). Per-class Booleans would admit a row claiming two grounds, which the instruction forbids.

Fact.Name: The firms a filer performed services for as a misclassified employee, one row per firm (Form 8919 lines 1-5)
Fact.Description:
The per-firm collection the printed lines 1-5 hold: "Complete a separate line for each firm" (line 148). Each row carries the six printed columns — (a) firm name, (b) federal identification number, (c) reason code, (d) date of the IRS determination, (e) the 1099-MISC/NEC checkbox, (f) wages — plus the spouse whose Form 8919 the row belongs on.
NO INTAKE ASKS IT TODAY, so an empty collection is the normal state and every committed scenario leaves it unanswered; the root then resolves Incomplete and is omitted from every snapshot. No dollar reads it — line 6 is column (f)'s attested total and keeps its own writable, for the reason argued in the section banner above.

Fact.Name: Column (a): the firm's name
Fact.Description:
Column (a) of the printed row. "Firm" is defined broadly by the instruction: "any individual, business enterprise, company, nonprofit organization, state, or other entity for which you performed services. This firm may or may not have paid you directly for these services" (lines 104-108) — which is why this is free text and not a link to any payer collection this dictionary already holds. When a Form 1099-MISC or 1099-NEC exists the instruction says to copy the name off it exactly (lines 70-73).
THE MaxLength BOUND MIRRORS formW2s:/formW2s/*/employerName; ITS Match REGEX IS DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED, for the reason given at form4137:/form4137Employers/*/writableEmployerName: that regex exists because the W-2 name feeds an MeF employer-name element, and this column is a line on a paper form rather than that element. A firm here can also be "any individual, business enterprise, company, nonprofit organization, state, or other entity", a broader set of names than an employer's, which makes importing the narrower character class worse here than there.

Fact.Name: Column (b): the firm's federal identification number, or the word "unknown"
Fact.Description:
Column (b) of the printed row. NOT A TYPED IDENTIFIER, and the instruction is why: the number "can be an employer identification number (EIN) or a social security number (SSN) (if the firm is an individual)", and "If you are unable to obtain the number, enter 'unknown'" (lines 75-86). Three shapes on one column, one of them a word — no EIN or TIN type can hold that, so it is carried as text bounded at 11 characters, the length of a formatted SSN (NNN-NN-NNNN), which is the longest of the three.
THE "unknown" ALTERNATIVE IS NOT A LOOPHOLE THIS DICTIONARY OPENS. It is the printed instruction's own answer to a firm that will not supply the number even after a Form W-9 request, which the same paragraph describes.

Fact.Name: Column (c): the reason code for filing Form 8919 against this firm
Fact.Description:
Column (c) of the printed row, over the closed set at /form8919ReasonCodeOptions. THIS IS THE ELIGIBILITY GROUND the printed who-must-file test requires: "One of the reasons listed below under Reason codes applies to you" (line 17).
IT IS ENFORCED by /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode, through ../isCodedRowForPrimaryFiler and ../isCodedRowForSecondaryFiler: a filer with positive line 6 and no answered column (c) anywhere on their own form is refused at submission. ANSWERED IS THE WHOLE TEST — no code is privileged, because the option set is closed and the instruction names G as the catch-all for a filer none of the others fit (lines 18-20). WHAT IS NOT ENFORCED, deliberately: an individual UNCODED row costs nothing while some sibling row of the same filer carries a code, because line 6 keeps its attested writable and the printed more-than-five-firms rule sanctions a partial table. That residual is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, because Form 8919 charges the employee half alone (6.2% + 1.45%) where a genuine independent contractor owes both halves as self-employment tax (12.4% + 2.9% on 92.35% of net earnings). Its bound is that the wages are an attestation either way: a filer who reaches this form without a ground has misreported income, not merely mis-selected a form, and nothing here manufactures a deduction or a credit.

Fact.Name: Column (d): the date of the IRS determination or correspondence
Fact.Description:
Column (d) of the printed row, "(d) Date of IRS determination or correspondence (MM/DD/YYYY)". The printed instruction makes it conditional: "Complete only if reason code A or C is entered in column (c)" (lines 135-137), which is carried as ../determinationDateRequired rather than left implicit.
UNANSWERED IS NOT REFUSED on any row. On a G or H row it is CORRECT to leave it blank — the instruction says to — and on an A or C row the omission is a filing-completeness question this module does not raise. The reason-code gate does NOT extend here: it tests only whether column (c) is answered SOMEWHERE on the filer's form, and a per-row date requirement would be a strictly stronger refusal with its own direction and its own witnesses. Line 6 is an attested total and no dollar here depends on the row.

Fact.Name: Column (d) must be completed on this row
Fact.Description:
The printed conditional on column (d): "Complete only if reason code A or C is entered in column (c)" (lines 135-137). True on an A or C row, false on a G or H row.
A REAL FACT RATHER THAN A COMMENT, because it is the only place the reason code drives anything at all today, and because the intake surface this collection exists to model is exactly where a conditional question belongs. It resolves Incomplete on a row whose reason code is unanswered, which is honest: without a code there is no answer to whether the date is required.

Fact.Name: Column (e): a Form 1099-MISC and/or 1099-NEC was received from this firm
Fact.Description:
Column (e) of the printed row, the checkbox "Check if Form 1099-MISC and/or 1099-NEC was received."
IT IS NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS REASON CODE H, and the two are easy to collapse. Code H requires BOTH a Form W-2 AND a 1099-MISC/NEC from the same firm, with the 1099 amount being wages that belonged on the W-2 (lines 102-108). This checkbox asks only whether a 1099 came at all, and it is printed as its own column on every row regardless of which code that row carries. Carried separately for that reason.

Fact.Name: Column (f): total wages received from this firm with no social security or Medicare tax withheld
Fact.Description:
Column (f) of the printed row: "Total wages received with no social security or Medicare tax withholding and not reported on Form W-2". Line 6 is this column's total.
LINE 6 READS THIS COLUMN when the filer's attested total is UNANSWERED, through the complete-safe addend ../wagesOrZero and the per-filer filtered views. An ANSWERED attested total still wins, for the more-than-five-firms reason the section banner gives. This writable is the PRINTED cell either way: the register maps /primaryFilerForm8919Firms/[n]/writableWages, never ../wagesOrZero.
SIGN: NON-NEGATIVE, carried as a declared Limit, matching /writablePrimaryFilerForm8919Wages.

Fact.Name: Column (f) for this row, complete-safe: the wages, or $0 when the cell is blank
Fact.Description:
The ADDEND form of column (f): ../writableWages when the cell is answered and $0 when it is not, so that the per-filer table totals /primaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal and /secondaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal stay Complete on a table whose rows are only partly filled in. Built to formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesUnrounded's shape, which is this dictionary's precedent for a complete-safe per-item addend.
CENTS ARE PRESERVED ON PURPOSE. This fact carries no Round; the single Round sits on /primaryFilerForm8919Line6 and /secondaryFilerForm8919Line6, which is what i1040gi page 23 requires of a line built by addition: "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total." Do NOT use this fact for the printed column (f) cell — the register prints ../writableWages.
THIS IS THE ADDEND, NOT THE CELL. It is summed by the two per-filer table totals, which line 6 combines when the attested total is unanswered and which /knockoutForm8919Line6BelowFirmTable compares an answered attested total against.

Fact.Name: Which spouse's Form 8919 this firm row belongs on
Fact.Description:
The per-row filer attribution, built to the shape scheduleH:/householdEmployees/*/writableEmployerFiler uses and matching form4137:/form4137Employers/*/writableEmployerFiler. Form 8919 is filed per spouse ("If married, complete a separate Form 8919 for each spouse who must file this form", line 10), so a firm row belongs to one spouse's form.
UNANSWERED IS THE PRIMARY FILER, exact for the single-form majority.

Fact.Name: This firm row is on the primary filer's Form 8919
Fact.Description: The primary half of the row attribution. AN UNANSWERED ../writableFirmFiler counts as the primary filer, for the reason given there.

Fact.Name: This firm row is on the secondary filer's Form 8919
Fact.Description:
The secondary half of the row attribution. It requires an ANSWERED ../writableFirmFiler, the mirror of ../belongsToPrimaryFiler's default, so that every row belongs to exactly one filer.
GUARDED ON /secondaryFiler'S OWN COMPLETENESS, which is what makes that "exactly one" claim true rather than merely intended. filers:/secondaryFiler is Find(/filers, isSecondaryFiler) and resolves INCOMPLETE on a return whose /filers holds a single item; a bare Equal against it is then Incomplete too, so an ANSWERED ../writableFirmFiler on such a return would carry that Incomplete into ../isCodedRowForSecondaryFiler, into the Count at /secondaryFilerHasForm8919ReasonCode, and out through /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode — a refusal that stops RESOLVING is not a refusal. The guard is the FIRST conjunct so the All short-circuits on it.
NO SUCH GUARD IS NEEDED ON THE PRIMARY SIDE and none is mirrored from it: filers:/primaryFiler is Complete on every return, which is already what keeps ../belongsToPrimaryFiler Complete. FALSE is the right fallthrough here on its own terms rather than by copying a precedent's polarity — where no secondary filer exists, no row belongs to one. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8919/f8919-reason-code-gate-single-filer-attributed-row-resolves.

Fact.Name: This row is on the primary filer's Form 8919 AND carries a reason code
Fact.Description:
The primary half of the eligibility-ground count. True when the row belongs to the primary filer (../belongsToPrimaryFiler, which takes an unanswered attribution as primary) AND its column (c) is ANSWERED.
ANSWERED, NOT ANY PARTICULAR CODE. The printed test is "One of the reasons listed below under Reason codes applies to you" (line 17) over a CLOSED four-value option set, so any answer at all satisfies it and no code is privileged. The instruction even names G as the catch-all for a filer none of the others fit (lines 18-20), which is why a code-specific test would be wrong here.
ALWAYS COMPLETE, which is what lets /primaryFilerHasForm8919ReasonCode Count these without an Incomplete item poisoning the count: ../belongsToPrimaryFiler is Complete on every row (its first disjunct is the unanswered case) and IsComplete is Complete by construction.

Fact.Name: This row is on the secondary filer's Form 8919 AND carries a reason code
Fact.Description:
Secondary-filer twin of ../isCodedRowForPrimaryFiler, over ../belongsToSecondaryFiler. Separate because Form 8919 is filed per spouse (line 10), so one spouse's coded row is no ground at all for the other spouse's wages.
ALWAYS COMPLETE, on the same requirement its twin records and for one more reason. The Count at /secondaryFilerHasForm8919ReasonCode returns Incomplete on ANY Incomplete element, so this fact being Complete on every row is a requirement rather than a convenience. IsComplete is Complete by construction, and ../belongsToSecondaryFiler is Complete on every row only because it carries an explicit guard on filers:/secondaryFiler, which is INCOMPLETE on a single-filer return where the primary twin's filers:/primaryFiler never is. That asymmetry is the whole of the difference between the two sides, and it is why this twin is not a mechanical copy.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Form 8919 total wages (line 6, column (f) total)
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's attested total of Form 8919 lines 1-5 column (f) — wages received from firms with no social security or Medicare tax withheld and not reported on a Form W-2.
SCREEN. Question: "What were [primary filer]'s total wages from firms that didn't withhold social security or Medicare tax?" Help text: this is Form 8919 line 6, "Total wages. Combine lines 1 through 5 in column (f)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8919.pdf, page 1). If the filer worked for MORE THAN FIVE such firms, the printed instruction is to enter the combined total of every firm, including the ones that do not fit on the five printed lines (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8919.pdf, page 2) — so this answer may be LARGER than the firm rows entered, and must never be smaller. ASKED-WHEN the return has any Form 8919 activity for this filer (the same intake that populates /form8919Firms). VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0, no Max. UNANSWERED POSTURE: optional — a filer who was never mistreated as a contractor never answers it and /primaryFilerForm8919Line6 falls through to the firm table and then to $0, so the return files with a blank Form 8919 line 6 and no Schedule 2 line 6 tax. FEEDS Form 8919 line 6, which feeds Form 1040 line 1g, Form 8959 line 3 and (through lines 10 to 13) Schedule 2 line 6.
IT IS NOT THE ONLY SOURCE OF LINE 6. This writable WINS whenever it is answered, but where it is UNANSWERED and /form8919Firms is answered, line 6 combines this filer's own column (f) rows, because that is what the printed line says.
TWO REFUSALS BOUND WHAT AN ANSWER CAN SAY, both at submission and neither silently altering the figure. (1) /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode: answering POSITIVE while /form8919Firms holds no coded row for this filer states Form 8919 wages with no printed ground. What survives is the PARTIAL table — one coded row grounds the whole attested amount, a taxpayer-FAVOURABLE residual, because Form 8919's employee-half rates are cheaper than the self-employment tax a genuine contractor owes. (2) /knockoutForm8919Line6BelowFirmTable: answering BELOW this filer's own column (f) rows prints a form that does not foot. The more-than-five-firms rule licenses larger and never smaller, so above and equal are admitted and only below is refused.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's Form 8919 total wages (line 6)
Fact.Description: Secondary-filer twin of /writablePrimaryFilerForm8919Wages. Separate because the form is filed per spouse.

Fact.Name: The primary filer's own column (f) rows, combined (Form 8919 lines 1 through 5)
Fact.Description:
The total of the column (f) cells on the firm rows attributed to the primary filer: CollectionSum over /primaryFilerForm8919Firms/*/wagesOrZero. This is what line 6's printed text combines, "Total wages. Combine lines 1 through 5 in column (f)."
ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT. Three places need it and none may recompute it: /primaryFilerForm8919Line6 combines it when the attested per-filer total is unanswered, /knockoutForm8919Line6BelowFirmTable compares the attested total against it, and /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode reads it to see whether this filer has stated any Form 8919 wages at all. Cents are preserved here for all three - line 6 carries the single Round, per i1040gi's rule that a line built by addition rounds the total and not the addends, and both knockouts compare raw attestation against raw table so a cent of rounding never manufactures or hides a footing failure.
COMPLETE-SAFE $0 when /form8919Firms is unanswered, which is the state of every return with no Form 8919 firm table. The guard is on the COLLECTION, a real "was the source answered" test, not on a complete-safe derived fact.
PER FILER, NOT PER RETURN: it sums the filtered view, never /form8919Firms, because Form 8919 is filed per spouse and one spouse's line 6 may never pick up the other's rows.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer's own column (f) rows, combined (Form 8919 lines 1 through 5)
Fact.Description:
Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal, summing /secondaryFilerForm8919Firms/*/wagesOrZero. See the primary twin for the one-quantity-one-fact argument, the cents rule and the complete-safe $0.
$0 ON A SINGLE-FILER RETURN rather than Incomplete, because /form8919Firms/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler guards filers:/secondaryFiler's own completeness and resolves Complete false where no secondary filer exists, so the filtered view is empty.

Fact.Name: Form 8919 line 6, primary filer (Form 1040 line 1g)
Fact.Description:
Form 8919 line 6: total wages from firms that withheld no social security or Medicare tax, the amount Form 1040 line 1g carries through income:/primaryFilerWagesFrom8919 and Form 8959 line 3 carries through /form8919Line6Total.
THREE ARMS, IN THIS ORDER. (1) The ATTESTED per-filer total, /writablePrimaryFilerForm8919Wages, whenever it is answered. (2) Otherwise, when /form8919Firms is answered, this filer's own column (f) rows combined - /primaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal - because line 6's printed text is "Total wages. Combine lines 1 through 5 in column (f)" and the table is then the return's only statement of the amount. (3) Otherwise the complete-safe $0, which keeps every return with no Form 8919 intake byte-identical.
WHY THE ATTESTED ARM IS FIRST. The printed more-than-five-firms rule tells a filer with six or more firms to attach additional Forms 8919 with lines 1 through 5 completed and to enter "the combined totals of all lines 1 through 5 of all your Forms 8919" on the one form's line 6, so the attested total may legitimately EXCEED the rows this collection prints and is the better statement of the line when the filer makes it. That rule defends the attested total winning when it is answered; it says nothing about a return that never answers it.
AND WHY WINNING IS NOT UNCONDITIONAL. The same rule licenses larger and never smaller, so an attested total BELOW this filer's own column (f) rows is a form that does not foot. It is refused at submission by /knockoutForm8919Line6BelowFirmTable rather than silently corrected here: the return has stated one quantity twice and this line takes the figure the filer stated, not a figure this dictionary preferred for him.
THE SECOND ARM'S PREDICATE is a real "was the source answered" test on a WRITABLE and on the intake COLLECTION, never an IsComplete on a complete-safe derived fact, which would always be true.
PER FILER, NOT PER RETURN, which is why the second arm reads the FILTERED view's total. Form 8919 is filed per spouse, so the primary filer's line 6 may never pick up a row attributed to the secondary filer; /secondaryFilerForm8919Line6 is the mirror, and the two views partition /form8919Firms because ../belongsToPrimaryFiler takes the unanswered attribution and ../belongsToSecondaryFiler requires an answered one.
NO ZERO FLOOR IS NEEDED, unlike Form 4137 lines 4 and 6: line 6 is a COMBINATION of column (f) amounts rather than a subtraction, and both the writable and /form8919Firms/*/writableWages carry a Min 0 limit, so no arrangement of valid inputs can drive it negative.
THE SINGLE Round IS DELIBERATE. /form8919Firms/*/wagesOrZero and /primaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal preserve cents so the Round applies to the total and not to each addend, which is what i1040gi page 23 requires of a line built by addition.

Fact.Name: Form 8919 line 6, secondary filer (Form 1040 line 1g)
Fact.Description:
Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerForm8919Line6. Same three arms in the same order: the attested /writableSecondaryFilerForm8919Wages when it is answered, else this filer's own column (f) rows combined (/secondaryFilerForm8919FirmTableTotal) when /form8919Firms is answered, else the complete-safe $0. See the primary twin for the printed line-6 text that proves the combination, for the more-than-five-firms rule that keeps the attested arm first, and for the footing guard that keeps it from winning below the table.
ITS FILTERED VIEW IS EMPTY, NOT INCOMPLETE, ON A SINGLE-FILER RETURN, which is what keeps this fact Complete at $0 there: /form8919Firms/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler guards filers:/secondaryFiler's own completeness and resolves Complete false when no secondary filer exists, so /secondaryFilerForm8919Firms filters to nothing and the sum is $0.

Fact.Name: Form 8919 line 6, both filers (Form 8959 line 3)
Fact.Description:
Both filers' Form 8919 line 6, summed — the amount Form 8959 line 3 carries. Form 8959 is a RETURN-level form while Form 8919 is filed per spouse, so the two per-filer line-6 figures add here, exactly as form4137:/form4137Line6Total does for line 2.
Complete-safe $0 on every return with no Form 8919 intake, which keeps Form 8959 line 4 and therefore Schedule 2 line 11 byte-identical on the committed corpus.

Fact.Name: The primary filer has stated a Form 8919 reason code on some firm row
Fact.Description:
True when at least one /form8919Firms row belonging to the primary filer has an answered column (c). This is the printed eligibility ground, counted.
THE FALLTHROUGH IS FALSE AND THAT POLARITY IS THE POINT. An unanswered /form8919Firms resolves Incomplete, and a bare Count over an absent collection resolves Placeholder rather than Complete, so the Count sits inside an IsComplete wrapper exactly as qbi:/qbiHasIncompleteQualifiedBusinesses and qbi:/qbiHasIneligibleAggregation do. Here the SAFE fallthrough is the opposite of theirs: an absent table means NO reason code has been stated, so the false arm must read "no ground", never "no problem". That is also the only shape today's intake can produce, since no screen asks the firm table yet, which makes this arm the population the gate actually meets rather than a corner case. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8919/f8919-reason-code-gate-no-table-one-dollar-refused.

Fact.Name: The secondary filer has stated a Form 8919 reason code on some firm row
Fact.Description:
Secondary-filer twin of /primaryFilerHasForm8919ReasonCode, over /form8919Firms/*/isCodedRowForSecondaryFiler. Separate because the form is filed per spouse.
ITS COUNT HAS ONE MORE WAY TO BE POISONED than the twin's, which is why the two are not symmetric below the surface. Every counted element must be Complete, and /form8919Firms/*/isCodedRowForSecondaryFiler is Complete on a single-filer return only because /form8919Firms/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler guards filers:/secondaryFiler, which is Incomplete there. Without that guard this fact resolved Incomplete on any return with one filer and an answered, attributed firm row, and carried the Incomplete out through /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8919/f8919-reason-code-gate-single-filer-attributed-row-resolves.

Fact.Name: A filer claims Form 8919 wages with no reason code stated anywhere
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when EITHER filer states positive Form 8919 wages - on line 6 OR in that filer's own firm rows - while having no coded firm row. The printed filing test is conjunctive and this is its fourth conjunct; the section banner above states what the predicate refuses, what it admits, and why it is a refusal rather than a zeroed line 6.
DIRECTION, and it is the reason this exists rather than a disclosure. Form 8919 charges the EMPLOYEE HALF alone: line 11 is line 10 x 0.062 and line 12 is line 6 x 0.0145 (lines 62-63). A genuine independent contractor owes BOTH halves as self-employment tax: Schedule SE line 10 is 12.4% and line 11 is 2.9%, on 92.35% of net earnings (Schedule SE lines 41-42). So an ungrounded Form 8919 claim is CHEAPER than the correct treatment, a taxpayer-FAVOURABLE under-collection, and the only false-allowance direction anywhere in this arc. It is bounded by the fact that the wages are an attestation either way: a filer who reaches this form without a ground has misreported income rather than merely mis-selected a form, and nothing here manufactures a deduction or a credit.
GATED BEHIND THE FILER'S OWN AFFIRMATIVE CLAIM, which is what makes the refusal safe. Line 6 is complete-safe $0, so a return that never answers ANY Form 8919 intake never reaches the test and is never refused (f8919-unanswered-complete-safe).
IT READS THE FIRM TABLE AND NOT ONLY LINE 6, and that is the difference between a guard and a guard that can be answered around. Line 6 takes the attested per-filer total whenever it is answered, so a filer who enters a firm row and then attests a total of $0 has a line 6 of $0 - and a predicate that read line 6 alone would see nothing while the return carried an ungrounded row in column (f). Each arm therefore fires on positive wages stated ANYWHERE for that filer: line 6 above zero OR /{primary,secondary}FilerForm8919FirmTableTotal above zero. The all-rows total is the right trigger, and a coded-only basis would be circular here because an UNCODED row is precisely the thing this test is looking for. The footing guard beside it reads the same total for its own reason - the register prints column (f) from every row in the view, so every row has to be footed. Witnessed by f8919-reason-code-gate-answered-zero-wages-uncoded-row-refused (attested $0.00 over an uncoded $500 row) and f8919-reason-code-gate-unanswered-wages-table-foots-refused (no attested total, one uncoded row).
MECHANISM: BlockSubmissionOnTrue and NO flow:/flowIsKnockedOut membership, which is a category judgment against lint_dual_wiring rather than a habit. That lint's permanent non-scope-guard exemption covers a refusal whose scope-sidecar revisit_trigger begins "n/a", and it applies here for the reason it applies to qbi:/qbiHasIneligibleAggregation: there is nothing unmodelled for a knockout SCREEN to explain. There is no Form 8919 computation this dictionary is failing to perform. The filer either states the printed ground or does not claim the wages, which is a user-input contradiction, and the refusal never retires.

Fact.Name: A filer's attested Form 8919 line 6 is less than his own column (f) rows
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when either filer ANSWERS his per-filer Form 8919 total below the combined column (f) of his OWN firm rows. Line 6's printed text is unconditional - "Total wages. Combine lines 1 through 5 in column (f)" - so a return whose line 6 is smaller than the rows printed above it does not foot, and the form it would print contradicts itself on its own face.
THE MORE-THAN-FIVE-FIRMS RULE IS WHY THIS IS ONE-SIDED, and it is the whole reason the comparison is LessThan rather than an equality. A filer with more than five firms attaches additional Forms 8919 with lines 1 through 5 completed and enters "the combined totals of all lines 1 through 5 of all your Forms 8919" on the one form's line 6. That licenses an attested total LARGER than the rows this return itemises; nothing printed anywhere licenses a smaller one. So an attested total above the table is admitted exactly as before, an attested total equal to it is admitted, and only below is refused.
IT MOVES NO DOLLAR. The attested arm of /primaryFilerForm8919Line6 still wins when it is answered, so line 6, Form 1040 line 1g, Form 8959 line 3 and Schedule 2 line 6 all keep the figure the filer stated. A refusal is the honest response because the return has made two contradictory statements of one quantity and this dictionary cannot know which is true: silently taking the larger would charge tax the filer never attested to, and silently taking the smaller is the under-collection this guard exists to stop.
EVERY ROW IN THE FILER'S VIEW, CODED OR NOT, and the printed page is the reason. The register maps the column (f) cell of rows 1 through 5 to /primaryFilerForm8919Firms/[0..4]/writableWages unconditionally, and column (c) is a separate cell, so a row whose reason code is blank still prints its wages on the face of the form. A line 6 below the rows printed above it therefore fails to foot whatever those rows' column (c) says, and a coded-only basis would admit a printed form that contradicts itself. Whether an uncoded row is grounded at all is the different question /knockoutForm8919WagesWithoutReasonCode asks, of the same total. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/form8919/f8919-line6-below-table-with-uncoded-row-refused, where the shortfall is created by an uncoded row beside a coded sibling and this guard fires alone.
COMPLETE-SAFE, AND THE ORDER OF THE CONJUNCTS IS WHAT MAKES IT SO. Each arm tests IsComplete on the per-filer writable FIRST, so the All short-circuits to false on the many returns that never answer it and the comparison is never evaluated against an Incomplete left side - a refusal that stops resolving is not a refusal.
